summary: An excerpt from a novel (labeled Book 6, part 107) in which a first-person narrator lies in bed in the dark with a man named Checker after sex. She tries to explain that she feels less desolate and untethered, but struggles to articulate her feelings and admits she is unsure whether she has had sex before. The conversation turns awkward as Checker is confused, and she deflects, saying she probably forgot. The passage is intimate and introspective, focused on emotional uncertainty rather than plot events.
one_line: A narrator lies awake beside Checker after sex, struggling to explain her feelings of comfort, confusion, and uncertain memories.
key_facts: The narrator tells Checker, "I don't want anything from you, either," and slides her hand over his very lightly.
Checker turns his hand under hers and interlaces their fingers, saying, "Yeah. Sure. We can do that."
The narrator says she feels "less desolate" with the warmth of another person beside her, though she does not feel exactly better.
The narrator says she felt "less untethered," and says this is not because of the sex, which she does not think is the important piece.
When the narrator says "Weird" aloud, Checker replies sleepily, "Well, I've had girls say worse."
Checker's goatee tickles the narrator's shoulder, and he smells like slightly burned plastic.
The narrator says, "I think this might have been the first time, for me," and admits she is not sure she has ever had sex before.
The narrator's memories of past sexual experiences are described as hazy, like mirages visible only out of the corner of her eye.
Checker says he is "just...confused," and the narrator notes they are reversing their conversation from the previous night.
The narrator says she thought she had had sex before but cannot pinpoint it, and says, "I probably forgot."
The narrator is unsure what she means by "this," which she describes as intimacy, friendship, and the idea that someone would catch her when she falls.
The narrator's breathing has slowed beside Checker, who appears to be falling asleep, while she stares up into the dark.

entities.name: Checker
entities.role: A man beside the narrator in bed, who holds her, comments humorously on her 'weird' remark, and expresses confusion about the conversation.
